target_customer: Remote and knowledge workers and students who want a focus workspace, mostly consumers using a free tier
problem: People struggle to focus when working from home; LifeAt combines task management with ambient video rooms, music, timers and virtual coworking.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription (monetization details not found)

founders.name: Devin Ajimine
founders.background_notes: YC page self-description: built prosumer products used by 10M+ users, content creator working with brands such as Google, Dropbox, Notion and Canva, Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree. No education or employers stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web and desktop app with embedded video content, timers, tasks and calendar sync; standard consumer app engineering, with video chat for coworking.

defensibility.rationale: Features such as focus timers, ambient video and coworking are easy to copy, and rivals like Focusmate and Flow Club existed; the only edge cited is creator-led distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sources show an incumbent copying or buying it; the app is still live.

market_need_then: Remote work after 2020 raised interest in focus tools and virtual coworking; the company claims 1M+ users at the time of YC and over 10M users later on its site, both self-reported.

identity.visual_style: Ambient lofi-style video rooms and calm focus scenes
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and mission-led about flow state

branding.brand_signature: Ambient focus spaces with video backgrounds
branding.community_and_virality: The company says its social accounts have 500K+ followers across TikTok, Instagram and Twitter and runs a program featuring user videos in its newsletter; WIRED wrote about remote coworking in August 2022, listed on the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Self-reported social following and creator-led marketing show brand-driven growth, though follower counts are unverified.

outcome_analysis: LifeAt grew through creator-led social distribution by its founder and raised about $3M in January 2023 from Meta and Line venture arms and others. It remains active, with a team of 6, but no revenue, retention or later rounds were found, so the evidence supports early traction rather than a proven business.
notes: The January 2023 round is labeled pre-seed by aggregators and seed in a company Notion page; stage set to other. GeekWire page returned 403 so investors and amount come from the search snippet and the YC page news line; Bouncewatch agrees on $3M. Bouncewatch also lists a $500K pre-seed in March 2022 (total $3.5M), unverified and not recorded. Competitor sources are 2023 comparison pages that describe products existing at founding; Flow Club founded 2021 per that source; Focusmate source undated. Focusmate (virtual coworking, named in the same comparison page) was left out because no dated source for it was found.
